title: My rights
lead: You can ask your bank to refund the annual card fee. Here you also see what paying only the minimum will cost you.
feesIntro: Banks must offer a card type without an annual fee. Below are the annual fees I found in your statements; choose one and I show where to apply and on what basis.
feeChooseLabel: Prepare a letter for the {{bank}} fee of {{date}}
feePick: Choose the fee you want back.
feeAllRefunded: Every fee I found has been refunded.
feeGone: This fee line is no longer stored.
feesEmptyTitle: I found no annual card fee in your statements
feesEmpty: When a statement has a card fee or membership fee line, I show it here with what you need to ask for it back.
letterIntro: Where to apply and the legal basis come from the data file. Check the current text at its source before you send anything.
routeLimitValue: in {{year}}, below {{limit}} goes to the arbitration committee
routeWhyHakem: The fee is below the limit. Write to the bank first; if that does not work, apply to the arbitration committee.
routeWhyCourt: The fee is above the limit. If the bank does not help, the next steps are mediation and then the consumer court.
letterHow: You can have the tool you chose write the letter here, or copy the prompt and give it to a tool you use yourself. Personal details stay as {{placeholders}}; you fill them in.
draftPending: Writing the letter. This can take more than a minute.
noProvider: To write it here, a commentary tool must be selected.
errProvider: The tool you chose is not running right now. You can copy the prompt and use it elsewhere.
errProviderFailed: The tool did not produce a letter. Try again in a moment.
errNetwork: I cannot reach the local server.
missingTitle: Some fields are missing from the draft
missingBody: These fields are not in the draft: {{list}}. Add them to the letter yourself.
letterHint: You can edit the text here. Copy and print use this version.
notStored: I do not store the letter or your personal details. The text is gone when you leave the page.
copyFailed: I could not copy. Select the text and copy it yourself.
minTitle: If I pay only the minimum
minIntro: The minimum payment does not close the debt; interest and taxes run on the part you put off. Code does the arithmetic; where each rate comes from is written beside it.
minEmpty: Once you upload a statement, I show how long the debt takes to close if you pay only the minimum, and what it costs you.
minGone: This statement is no longer stored.
minSentence_one: Paying only the minimum, the {{balance}} debt takes {{count}} statement to close, with the last payment at the {{date}} cut-off. That is <c>{{cost}}</c> more than paying it all at once.
minSentence_other: Paying only the minimum, the {{balance}} debt takes {{count}} statements to close, with the last payment at the {{date}} cut-off. That is <c>{{cost}}</c> more than paying it all at once.
minSentenceOpen_one: Paying only the minimum, the {{balance}} debt is still open after {{count}} statement; <c>{{left}}</c> remains.
minSentenceOpen_other: Paying only the minimum, the {{balance}} debt is still open after {{count}} statements; <c>{{left}}</c> remains.
minBarCaption: The first slice is the debt itself; the grey slices are the interest and taxes added if you pay only the minimum. Paying it all now costs {{full}}.
ratesChange: If your bank charges you a different rate, change it in Settings.
assume_minimum_paid_on_time: Every minimum is paid in full by its due date, so no late interest runs.
assume_interest_on_unpaid_only: Interest runs only on the unpaid part, for the real days between cut-offs.
assume_rates_follow_caps: The rate is the one printed on your statement, never above the TCMB maximum for the date.
assume_scheduled_installments_added: Scheduled installments are added to the month they fall in.
assume_no_new_spending: The card is not used again until the debt is gone.
assume_cut_off_day_kept: Later cut-off dates keep this statement's day of the month.
cyclesCaption: Debt, minimum payment and interest added, statement by statement
